title: GE Vernova T&D India in focus as Power Grid secures 6000 MW Barmer HVDC project
text: GE Vernova T&D India said it has received a letter dated 7 September 2026 from Power Grid Corporation of India intimating that the company has emerged as the L1 bidder for the design and establishment of a 6,000 MW, 800 kV High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) LCC Terminal Station (2x3000 MW) for evacuation of renewable power from Barmer II in Rajasthan to South Kalamb in Maharashtra. Power Grid Corporation of India officially secured the developer contract for the inter-state transmission system on 2 September 2026. The broader scheme comprises 6,000 MW HVDC terminals at Barmer-II and South Kalamb, a roughly 1,000-km HVDC bipole line, 400 kV transmission lines and two synchronous condenser units. The proposed assignment involves the design, supply and execution of a 6,000 MW, plus-minus 800 kV HVDC Line Commutated Converter terminal station, configured as two 3,000 MW terminals. Revenue recognition from the assignment is likely to begin around FY29. GE Vernova T&D India is one of the few companies in the country with a local HVDC line commutated converter manufacturing line.
